sections.title: $ whoami
lines: Software engineer since 1995. Hardware install and help desk before ever writing a line of code.
Learned HTML. Then JavaScript. Then server-side web. Then SQL. Then enterprise CMS. Then JS again.
Led teams. Mentored engineers. Became a manager.
Spent the last decade teaching junior devs to work on systems they didn't build and don't fully
understand. Turns out that is exactly the skill you need to work with AI.

sections.title: $ ./ai-operator.sh
lines: [AI OPERATOR]
The 30 years matter: knowing what to ask for, when output is wrong, how to hand off complex work.
Think of the Operators in The Matrix — not jacked in, sitting in the real world, reading the data.
They upload what the crew needs, monitor what's happening inside, pull the cord when things go wrong.
Not inside the AI blindly accepting output. Above it — reading, directing, correcting, shaping.
The contribution graph has exploded. The output is real. The craft directing it is still mine.
Tools change. Notepad became an IDE. The IDE became an AI pair. The craft stays the same.
